sentences.text: The holotype specimen IGM 100/1321 — the specific fossil the species is based on — preserves the back of the skull, lower jaws, neck vertebrae, parts of the front limbs, and bony armor plates.
Its skull was relatively wide, with upper openings completely closed by surrounding bones, a trait shared with other gobiosuchids.
The animal possessed highly developed bony armor plates, featuring four rows of dorsal plates fused together, each with a sharp spike and rough ridges.
Neck armor plates were likely fused to back plates to form a complete concentric ring of protection around the neck, torso, and tail.
Its long and slender front limbs suggest it may have been adapted for a terrestrial lifestyle rather than swimming.
Researchers classified it as the closest relative to Gobiosuchus kielanae, sharing 14 key skull features that define the family Gobiosuchidae.
It lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
